findings.summary: INV-8 claims no file can be both `unmodeled` and paired, but `unmodeled_markdown` never filters out docs declared by a config pair's `docs` glob (unlike orphan detection, which does).
findings.evidence: Doc INV-8: "Every path in `unmodeled` sits in a directory holding no candidate code file, so no file is ever both unmodeled and paired." (with §2: "Pair | `{label, code[], docs[]}` — links code globs to spec doc(s)"). Code `unmodeled_markdown` filters only on `if d in code_dirs: continue`, `classify_exclude(md, user_excludes) == "user"`, and `CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS`; there is no `pair_docs` check, whereas the orphan pass explicitly has `if md in pair_docs: continue`. Verified: config `pairs=[{code:['src/a.py'], docs:['spec/*.md']}]` over a repo with `src/a.py` + `spec/FR-1..3.md` returns `covered: ['src/a.py']` and `unmodeled: [{dir:'spec', files:3, ...}]` — the same three files are both pair-declared docs and reported as unmodeled.
findings.suggestion: Either pass `pair_docs` into `unmodeled_markdown` and skip pair-declared docs (mirroring the orphan pass), or reword INV-8 to drop the "so no file is ever both unmodeled and paired" clause and state only the directory-has-no-candidate-code rule that the code actually enforces.

verification.doc_quote: A file qualifies when it sits in a directory holding no candidate code, is not user-excluded, and is not a conventional doc name.
verification.why: The §3 "Unmodeled markdown detection" narrative states the qualification rule exactly as the code implements it (three conditions, no pair-docs filter), so INV-8's trailing "so no file is ever both unmodeled and paired" is a loose restatement of the same-stem pairing model ("Markdown that same-stem pairing cannot reach"), not a separate contradicted claim about config pairs.
